account.title.note: The account page's section about push notifications

account.browser.note: The switch that turns notifications on in the browser the reader is using

account.allowAgain.message: To allow them again: click the site settings icon left of the address, set Notifications to Allow, then reload this page.
account.allowAgain.note: Shown when the browser blocked notifications for the site

account.turnOff.note: A link next to one of the reader's other browsers

ios.title.message: To get notifications, add {site} to your Home Screen: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
ios.title.note: iPhone and iPad: web push works only for sites added to the Home Screen. site: The Acme newsletter

ios.open.message: Open {site} from the Home Screen and allow notifications

preferences.turnOff.message: Turn off notifications in this browser
preferences.turnOff.note: A button on the preference center

preferences.done: Notifications are off in this browser.
preferences.none: This browser doesn't get notifications from this site.

browser.chrome_android.note: One of the reader's browsers on the account page, before “on since 9 Oct”

public.linkGone.message: This notification's link is no longer valid.
public.linkGone.note: The page a reader gets when they click an expired or unknown notification

prompt.title.note: A new push prompt's title, which the site's readers see until the member rewrites it

prompt.message: One notification when a new post is out. Never more than one a day.

prompt.allow.note: A new push prompt's button that asks the browser for permission

label.publicationSite.note: The label of the workspace's publication website in Push setup's sites

label.copyOf.note: The name of a duplicated push campaign; name is the original's

notify.workerMissing.title.note: A notification to members: host is the site (help.acme.io)

notify.workerMissing.summary.message: {url} {answer, select, none {didn't answer} other {answered {status}}} · notifications to {count, plural, one {# subscriber} other {# subscribers}} are held
notify.workerMissing.summary.note: url: where the worker should answer (https://help.acme.io/rc-push-sw.js); status: the HTTP status it answered (404); answer is none when the site didn't answer at all

notify.workerMissing.body.message: {url} {answer, select, none {didn't answer} other {answered {status}}}. Notifications to {host}'s {count, plural, one {# subscriber} other {# subscribers}} are held, and new subscriptions there fail, until the file is back. Upload {file} to the site's root, then check again in Push setup.

problem.alreadyOn: Push is already on for this workspace.
problem.contact: Enter an email address or an https:// address the push services can reach you at.
problem.contactNoKeys: Turn push on first: the contact goes with the keys.
problem.noKeysToRotate: Push isn't on: there are no keys to rotate.

problem.rotateConfirm.message: Type {n} to confirm: that's how many subscriptions end.
problem.rotateConfirm.note: n: the number of subscriptions, without separators (4264)

problem.siteAddress: Enter the site's address, like help.acme.io. Browsers allow notifications only from https sites.
problem.siteNoKeys: Turn push on first: sites use the workspace's keys.
problem.workerPath: Enter the worker's path on the site, like /rc-push-sw.js or /sw.js.
problem.pickImage: Pick an image from the media library.

problem.pickIds.message: Pick {what, select, sites {sites} lists {lists} segments {segments} other {{what}}} of this workspace.
problem.pickIds.note: what the campaign's audience was given that isn't the workspace's

problem.pickSites: Pick sites of this workspace's push setup.

problem.link.message: Enter the address the notification opens, like {example}.
problem.link.note: example: an address such as news.acme.io/p/feature-flags, never translated

problem.notEditable.message: This campaign is {status, select, scheduled {scheduled} sending {sending} paused {paused} sent {sent} cancelled {cancelled} failed {failed} other {{status}}}: it can't be edited any more.

problem.staleVersion.message: Someone saved version {version} since you opened it. Reload to see their changes.

problem.button: A button needs a label and the address it opens.

problem.scheduleLocked.message: This campaign is {status, select, scheduled {scheduled} sending {sending} paused {paused} sent {sent} cancelled {cancelled} failed {failed} other {{status}}}: its schedule can't change.

problem.futureTime: Pick a time in the future.

problem.alreadySent.message: This campaign is already {status, select, scheduled {scheduled} sending {sending} paused {paused} sent {sent} cancelled {cancelled} failed {failed} other {{status}}}.

problem.changedSinceReview.message: The campaign changed since you reviewed it (now version {version}). Review it again.

problem.blockingChecks: Fix the blocking checks before sending.
problem.unschedule: Only a scheduled campaign that hasn't started can go back to a draft.
problem.cancel: Only a scheduled or sending campaign can be cancelled.
problem.testNoKeys: Turn push on first: the test is signed with the workspace's keys.
problem.testSubscription: This browser's subscription can't be used: allow notifications for this page and try again.
problem.testTitle: Write the title first: a notification needs one.
problem.promptSite: Pick one of the workspace's push sites.
problem.promptPushOff: Turn push on in Sending providers › Push first: the prompt subscribes readers with the workspace's keys.
problem.promptNotPushSite: The prompt's site isn't a push site yet. Add it in Push setup; readers can't subscribe until it is.
problem.promptUnchanged: Nothing new to publish: readers see these settings.
problem.promptDraft: Publish the prompt first: a draft has nothing to pause.
problem.promptStyle: Pick a style: slide-in bar, dialog or bell button.

problem.promptTitleLength.message: Keep the title to {max, number} characters.

problem.promptMessageLength.message: Keep the message to {max, number} characters.

problem.promptWhen: Check at least one rule for when the prompt shows.
problem.promptScroll: Scrolling is a percent of the post, 1 to 100.
problem.promptPath: Paths start with / and are part of the site's addresses, like /account.
problem.promptPages: Add the pages the prompt shows on.

webhook.push.clicked.message: A reader clicked a notification or one of its buttons (once per notification).
webhook.push.clicked.note: a webhook event, in Settings › Webhooks
